clue.text: Tex with duo performing in evening wear

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cowboy called Tex and his double act are dressed up for an evening show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' is the anagram signal for TEX and DUO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuxedo is a dinner jacket, the formal outfit worn for evening functions.

clue.text: Me in person entering academy self-consciously

indicators.note: the answer is entering, i.e. sitting inside, the words academy self-consciously

explanation.surface: Someone feels awkward walking into a college in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the letters run across the end of 'academy' and the start of 'self-consciously'.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun stresses the speaker personally, 'I myself', so it means 'me in person'.

clue.text: Highwayman upset and he took fright

indicators.note: upset tells us the following letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A highwayman is thrown into confusion when his victim panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is the anagram signal for all of AND HE TOOK FRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Knight of the road is an old romantic euphemism for a mounted robber who held up coaches.

clue.text: Sort prepared and ready for printing

parts.note: sort as a noun means kind or type
prepared means set, as in all set

explanation.surface: Something is arranged and made ready to go to press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' is also a printer's term for a piece of type, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Typeset copy has been composed into type, so it is set up and ready to be printed.

clue.text: Giving support to sentence existing now

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
a prison sentence is the time served, as in doing the time
existing means being, in existence

explanation.surface: Backing a punishment that is currently in force.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at present or temporarily, describing how things stand at this moment.

clue.text: I am conforming strictly to convention although unfit

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
proper means correct and conventional in behaviour

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be very correct and conventional even though they are not up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means unsuitable or inappropriate, which is what unfit means in this sense.

clue.text: Brief us, up before County Council in court

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word us is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: CC is the standard abbreviation for County Council

explanation.surface: A lawyer is briefing clients before a local council hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means read backwards; 'Brief' looks like a verb to a lawyer but is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Succinct means concise and to the point, which is what brief means as an adjective.

clue.text: Youngster reported party facing variable resistance

indicators.note: reported means the word for youngster is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a youngster is a boy
the ANC, African National Congress, is the South African political party
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A young man faces an electorate of uncertain resistance to his party.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY said out loud gives BUOY, the floating marker.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyancy is the upward force a fluid exerts against sinking, a resistance to going under.

clue.text: Thus on the way back, mother carries one heavy metal

indicators.note: on the way back means the word for thus is read in reverse

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: carries means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: mum is mother
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother on a return journey lugs a heavy load of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: SO reversed gives OS; MUM 'carries' I to give MIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, a hard metallic one.

clue.text: Two I will leave in state of equality

indicators.note: will leave signals that the letter I is taken out of the word for two

parts.note: a pair is two

explanation.surface: Two people agree to an even split, with one walking out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a par means being level or equal, so par is the condition of equality.

clue.text: From ESE, a gale confused flighty creature

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strong wind from the east-south-east throws a bird off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' is the anagram signal for ESE, A and GALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea eagle is a large fish-eating raptor, a creature that flies, hence 'flighty' playfully.

clue.text: Three times heretic turns, losing direction

indicators.note: turns means the letters of heretic are turned about into another order
losing means a letter is dropped from the result

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A heretic changes sides three times and loses his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' scrambles HERETIC and 'losing' drops one E.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrice is an old-fashioned word for on three occasions.

clue.text: Become angry, leave part of pool

parts.note: to go off is to leave
the deep end is the part of a swimming pool where the water is deepest

explanation.surface: A swimmer is told to get out of the deep water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper suddenly and fly into a rage.

clue.text: Acceptable to include American tall plant

indicators.note: to include means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: An American tall plant is approved.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak is a large tree, and a tree is a tall plant.

clue.text: Dissolute character away with their share?

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man of loose morals
off means away, as in off on holiday

explanation.surface: A libertine makes off with his cut of the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with their' are link words; the question mark hints the share may be ill-gotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a cut or commission, often dishonest, taken from profits.

clue.text: Only just enough now to represent as comparable

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, so now
to equate things is to treat them as equal or comparable

explanation.surface: A description of how to compare two things that are barely sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means sufficient but no more, satisfactory without being good.

clue.text: Regular air service

parts.note: even means regular or steady
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A routine flight run by an airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air service' suggests an airline; the definition is church worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, sung in many churches.

clue.text: Shake badly-behaved child held by rival

indicators.note: held by means the second piece is held within the first

parts.note: to vie is to rival or compete
a brat is a badly-behaved child

explanation.surface: A naughty child is shaken by a competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to move to and fro rapidly, to quiver or tremble.

clue.text: Drink, light without head

indicators.note: without head means the word for light loses its first letter

parts.note: pale means light in colour

explanation.surface: A light drink served with no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' plays on the froth on a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a kind of beer, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Train Jo to work as attendant

indicators.note: to work means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trainee called Jo is being taught to work as an attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' is the anagram signal for TRAIN JO.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a caretaker or doorkeeper who attends to a building.

clue.text: Flat-topped cool?

parts.note: level-headed read literally is a head that is level or flat on top; the quality of keeping calm is a cool head

explanation.surface: A query about something with a flat top that is calm.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means calmness and good sense, keeping composure under pressure.

clue.text: Off about one? That's the idea

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: something off is not on, as in that's not on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure about one thing, then the idea dawns.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, a thought held in the mind.

clue.text: Seat almost fixed

indicators.note: almost means the word for fixed loses its last letter

parts.note: settled means fixed or decided

explanation.surface: A chair is nearly repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a wooden bench with a high back and arms.

clue.text: Money's right for naval officer

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money, such as prize money

explanation.surface: Cash is just the thing for a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A purser is the ship's officer in charge of accounts and stores.

clue.text: I had existence and personality

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
an entity is something with real existence

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have had both existence and character.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity is the sense of who a person is, their individual character.

clue.text: Cannot be considered back in the pavilion

definitions.meaning: an idea that is ... is ... of the question, not to be considered
in cricket a dismissed batsman is ... and walks back to the pavilion, the clubhouse

explanation.surface: A rejected suggestion is like a batsman returning to the clubhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: ruled out of consideration, and dismissed from batting in cricket.

clue.text: Way a New Zealander initially has with a few lines

parts.note: St, street, is a way

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of New and Zealander are taken

explanation.surface: A New Zealander composes a short verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Personal aspirations that are mistakes

parts.note: own means personal, belonging to oneself
goals are aspirations or aims

explanation.surface: One's individual ambitions turn out to be errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Own goals are self-inflicted blunders, from the football sense of scoring against one's own side.
